label: Useful
description: Genera with well-documented benefits for crops or soil fertility.

label: Nutrient suppliers
description: Make nutrients available to crops; use directly only when no child fits (e.g. potassium or iron mobilisation).

label: Nitrogen fixers
description: Turn nitrogen gas from the air into ammonium, free-living in soil or loosely associated with grass roots.

label: Legume nodule partners
description: Rhizobia that fix nitrogen inside root nodules of soybean, alfalfa, beans and other legumes.

label: Phosphorus solubilisers
description: Free phosphorus bound in minerals or organic matter with acids, phosphatases or phytases.

label: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi
description: Glomeromycota fungi that live in crop roots and extend them to reach phosphorus and water.

label: Growth promoters
description: Promote root or plant growth directly; use directly only when no child fits (e.g. induced systemic resistance).

label: Root stress relievers
description: Carry ACC deaminase, which lowers the stress hormone ethylene in roots under drought, heat or salt.

label: Plant hormone makers
description: Make auxin, gibberellin or cytokinin in amounts shown to change root or shoot growth.

label: Pest and disease suppressors
description: Hold crop pathogens or pests in check; use directly only when no child fits (e.g. competition for roots or iron).

label: Antimicrobial producers
description: Make antifungal or antibacterial compounds (e.g. DAPG, hydrogen cyanide, phenazines, lipopeptides) that suppress root pathogens.

label: Parasites of other fungi
description: Attack and feed on other fungi, crop pathogens included (e.g. Trichoderma, Clonostachys).

label: Chitin digesters
description: Notable for breaking down chitin of fungal walls and insect shells, which can weaken fungal pathogens.

label: Insect and nematode enemies
description: Kill or trap insect pests or plant-parasitic nematodes (e.g. Bacillus thuringiensis, Beauveria, Metarhizium).

label: Potentially harmful
description: Genera that include species harmful to crops, livestock or people.

label: Genera with plant pathogens
description: Include species that cause crop or plant diseases; use directly only when the disease type is unclear or mixed.

label: Root and soilborne pathogens
description: Cause root, crown, tuber or seedling rots, damping-off, scab, or wilts that enter through the roots.

label: Leaf, stem, head and seed pathogens
description: Cause leaf spots, blights, rusts, head blight, stalk or ear rots; soil and crop residue serve as their reservoir.

label: Mycotoxin producers
description: Include species that can leave toxins in grain or forage (e.g. deoxynivalenol, fumonisins, aflatoxins).

label: Human or animal pathogens
description: Include species that cause disease in people or livestock, mostly opportunistic infections from soil, dust or manure.

label: Nitrogen cyclers
description: Move nitrogen between forms; good or bad for the crop depending on timing, water and fertiliser management.

label: Nitrifiers
description: Turn ammonium into nitrite and nitrate (ammonia- and nitrite-oxidising bacteria and archaea, comammox Nitrospira); nitrate feeds crops but can leach.

label: Denitrifiers
description: Turn nitrate into nitrogen gases, a nitrogen loss and a source of the greenhouse gas N2O, mostly in wet soil.

label: N2O reducers
description: Turn the greenhouse gas N2O into harmless nitrogen gas (N2), the last step of denitrification.

label: Nitrate-to-ammonium (DNRA)
description: Turn nitrate back into ammonium, which stays in the soil instead of leaching or escaping as gas.

label: Neutral / background
description: Ordinary soil life with no direct and well-documented effect on crops.

label: Decomposers
description: Notable for breaking down crop residues and organic matter (saprotrophs), recycling nutrients.

label: Endophytes
description: Live inside plant tissues without known disease; effect on the crop unclear.

label: Tree mycorrhizal fungi
description: Ecto-, ericoid or orchid mycorrhizal fungi that partner with trees or shrubs, not with field crops.

label: Common soil microbes
description: Known, often common soil microbes with no specific crop-related role.

label: Role unknown
description: Too little is known about the genus to give it a role.

label: Probably misnamed reads
description: Genus not expected in cropland soil (e.g. obligate insect symbionts, hyperthermophiles, extreme halophiles); reads are likely misassigned or incidental.
